newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso chooses new parliament.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso chooses new parliament.

text.p: Burkina Faso voted for a new national assembly on Sunday with President Blaise Compaore's ruling party the only one putting up candidates nationwide but with little sign of enthusiasm in the country's two main cities.
Witnesses reported a low turnout in the capital Ouagadougou and the second city Bobo-Dioulasso. Many voters in the capital experienced problems with their voter cards, they said.

Compaore predicted that more voters would turn out later. "This shows that Burkinabe (citizens) are keen to consolidate democracy while taking care of their day-to-day problems at the same time as the future of the country," he said after voting.
State television showed long queues of voters in towns outside Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso.

Compaore's ruling Congress for Popular Democracy (CDP) held 88 out of 107 seats in the outgoing national assembly, which was elected in 1992 during the landlocked West African nation's return to multi-party politics.
Parliament amended the constitution in January to increase the size of the assembly to 111.
Opposition leaders, while hoping for victory, say they would be content with an increased stake in the new parliament.
"We hope that the opposition wins a majority in the national assembly," Professor Joseph Ki-Zerbo, leader of the Party for Democracy and Progress (PDP), said on the eve of polling.
"If that is not possible, we hope for a blocking minority, to propose and transform, slowly but surely towards a new Burkina Faso," he added.
Thirteen parties and 569 candidates took part on Sunday.
Burkina Faso's 4.8 million voters had until 6 p.m. (1800 GMT) to vote. Election officials predicted first results on Sunday night and final provisional results by Wednesday.
Compaore came to power in a 1987 army coup in which populist leader Thomas Sankara, his former close friend, was killed.
The constitution initially limited him to one seven-year term. Parliament in January voted to let him stand as many times as he wants. The next presidential election is due in 1998.
Cash-strapped opposition parties staged modest campaigns. The ruling party held more than 100 rallies in the Ouagadougou area alone.
Opposition parties made allegations of widespread malpractice and fraud at the last election.

"We have to hope that those who last time put a lot more effort into fraud than into fair competition will be more above board this time," said Sebastian Ouedraogo, secretary general of the opposition Alliance for Democracy and Federation recently.

Under pressure from Western donors for democratic reform in the early 1990s, Compaore underwent a lightning conversion to multi-party politics and was elected as the sole candidate in 1991 elections -- which opposition parties boycotted as unfair.

Burkina Faso, locked in the arid Sahel belt, exports livestock to its neighbours and increasing quantities of green beans and other fruit and vegetables to Europe. Gold mining is on the rise and plans are afoot to mine zinc and manganese.
